{{Short description|Generalization of natural transformations}}In [[category theory]], a branch of [[mathematics]], a '''dinatural transformation''' <math>\alpha</math> between two [[functor]]s

:<math>S,T : C^{\mathrm{op}}\times C\to D,</math>

written

:<math>\alpha : S\ddot\to T,</math>

is a function that to every object <math>c</math> of <math>C</math> associates an arrow

:<math>\alpha_c : S(c,c)\to T(c,c)</math> of <math>D</math>

and satisfies the following [[coherence property]]: for every morphism <math>f:c\to c'</math> of <math>C</math> the diagram
[[Image:Dinatural transfo1.png|center]]
commutes.<ref>{{cite book|url={{Google books|gfI-BAAAQBAJ|page=218|plainurl=yes}}  |last1=Mac Lane |first1=Saunders |author-link = Saunders Mac Lane|title=Categories for the working mathematician |date=2013 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |page=218}}</ref> Note the direction of <math>S(f,g)</math> is opposite along  <math>f</math> in the first component since it is contravariant. 

The composition of two dinatural transformations need not be dinatural.
